question.problem:
Given the arithmetic sequence 

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-6,\,{a}_{1}=2,\,n\ge 1,
$$

the index of the term $-124$ is $n=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We will convert the recursive formula to an explicit formula and then solve for the value of $n$ such that ${a}_{n}=-124.$

The recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence takes the form

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+d.
$$

In the given formula, we have $d=-6.$ We are also told that ${a}_{1}=2,$ so we can write the explicit formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =2+(n-1)(-6) \\  & =2-6n+6 \\  & =-6n+8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ such that ${a}_{n}=-124:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-6n+8 \\ -124 & =-6n+8 \\ -132 & =-6n \\ \frac{-132}{-6} & =n \\ 22 & =n \\ n & =22\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $-124$ is the $22$nd term of the sequence.
